metadata.title: Evolution of Quantum Computing: Theoretical and Innovation Management Implications for Emerging Quantum Industry

problem_domains.problem: Evolution of quantum computing research and technologies
problem_domains.description: The paper addresses how quantum computing research is developing over time to support scientific advances and technological change.
problem_domains.quote: One of the fundamental questions hardly known is how quantum computing research is developing to support scientiﬁc advances and the evolution of path-breaking technologies for economic, industrial, and social change.

problem_domains.problem: Detection of main quantum computing technologies and trajectories
problem_domains.description: The study seeks to detect main QC technologies and technological trajectories that may become major sources of competitive advantage.
problem_domains.quote: This study can detect the main QC technologies, which may be major sources of competitive advantage for ﬁrms and nations to solve complex problems and satisfy new needs of people in society.

problem_domains.problem: Lack of scientometric studies on evolutionary networks of quantum computing
problem_domains.description: The paper notes a scarcity of scientometric analyses of QC evolutionary networks associated with new technologies.
problem_domains.quote: However, studies of scientometrics concerning evolutionary networks of QC associated with new technologies are scarce in the literature.

problem_domains.problem: Guiding R&D investments and innovation strategy in quantum technologies
problem_domains.description: The work addresses how to guide R&D and innovation strategy by understanding QC evolution and emerging technologies.
problem_domains.quote: The results of these studies can guide R&D investments and innovation strategy of ﬁrms and governments for supporting their competitive advantage in turbulent markets [33]–[37].

problem_domains.problem: Identifying emerging quantum technologies for innovative applications in markets
problem_domains.description: The study focuses on identifying emerging QC technologies that can be transferred into innovative market applications.
problem_domains.quote: This result suggests the potential transfer of QC research in new technologies for innovative applications, such as in quantum image processing for creating quantum images because this new technology has high technical performance in terms of computing speed, low storage requirements, and high security [56].

problem_domains.problem: Supporting strategic management of innovation for a quantum industry
problem_domains.description: The paper addresses how understanding QC evolution can support strategic innovation management and the emergence of a quantum industry.
problem_domains.quote: the results presented here clearly illustrate the main evolutionary paths of QC research that are increasingly based on growing connectivity between technologies and research ﬁelds, but a further detailed examination is needed for explaining the driving factors of the technological evolution and supporting an appropriate strategic management of innovation that supports a new quantum industry for the competitive advan- tage of ﬁrms and nations in turbulent markets.

solution_approaches.description: The authors apply computational scientometric methods on publication data to explain the structure and evolution of quantum computing research and technologies.
solution_approaches.quote: This study confronts the question here by applying methods of computational scientometrics for publication analyses to explain the structure and evolution of quantum computing research and technologies over a 30-year period.

solution_approaches.approach: Maps of science / mapping of QC networks
solution_approaches.description: The study creates and analyzes maps of science based on keyword co-occurrence networks to show how QC fields and technologies evolve.
solution_approaches.quote: This study endeavors to create and analyze the mapping of QC over a 30-year time frame to detect different stages of the structure of network and the evolution of QC with main technological trajectories.

solution_approaches.approach: Keyword co-occurrence networks using DE tags
solution_approaches.description: The authors construct keyword co-occurrence networks from Web of Science author keywords (DEs) to identify QC research fields and technologies.
solution_approaches.quote: First, we used original keywords of articles (DEs) tag as the basis for detection of technologies related to QC. ... the units of analysis are the original keywords (DEs) of articles provided by authors to ﬁnd the QC research ﬁelds and technolo- gies and to create the interconnection network among nodes.
solution_approaches.location: Materials and Method, Section B, Page 2

solution_approaches.description: The study uses degree, betweenness, and closeness centrality metrics to explore evolutionary behavior of nodes in the QC network.
solution_approaches.quote: Moreover, SCI2 Tool is applied to calculate metrics of these networks, such as degree centrality (DC), betweenness centrality (BC), and closeness centrality (CC) measures to explore the evolutionary behavior of different nodes within the network of QC over time.
solution_approaches.location: Materials and Method, Section C, Page 3

solution_approaches.description: The network is analyzed in three time periods to study changes in structure, connectivity, and emerging technologies.
solution_approaches.quote: The sample contains 14,132 articles split into three timespans, given by 1990–2000, 2001–2010, and 2011–2020.
solution_approaches.location: Materials and Method, Section A, Page 2

solution_approaches.approach: Identification of emerging technologies via network connectivity
solution_approaches.description: Emerging QC technologies are identified based on their appearance and connectivity patterns in the network over time.
solution_approaches.quote: The emerging technologies in QC from 2001 to 2010 are (see Table IV): quantum memory, adiabatic QC, topological QC, quantum walk, and quantum wire. Furthermore, over 2011- 2020, the emerging technologies are quantum image processing, quantum machine learning, and blind QC.

solution_approaches.description: The authors analyze the morphological evolution of the QC network from spheroid to irregular shapes to characterize stages of scientific and technological evolution.
solution_approaches.quote: Theoretical implications of this study show the morphological evolution of the network in quantum computing from a symmetric to an asymmetric shape driven by new inter-related research ﬁelds and emerging technolog- ical trajectories.

solution_approaches.approach: Innovation management guidance based on network metrics
solution_approaches.description: The study proposes using network measures (e.g., high degree centrality nodes) to guide R&D investment and innovation management decisions.
solution_approaches.quote: Findings here suggest best practices of innovation management based on R&D investments in new technological di- rections of quantum computing having a high potential for growth and impact in science and markets.

problem_solution_mappings.problem: Supporting strategic management of innovation for a quantum industry
problem_solution_mappings.quote: Despite these limitations, the results presented here clearly illustrate the main evolutionary paths of QC research that are increasingly based on growing connectivity between technologies and re- search ﬁelds, but a further detailed examination is needed for explaining the driving factors of the technological evolution and supporting an appropriate strategic management of innovation that supports a new quantum industry for the competitive advan- tage of ﬁrms and nations in turbulent markets.

key_claims.claim: Quantum computing research is rapidly evolving with increasing network connectivity and complexity over 1990–2020.
key_claims.quote: Results reveal that the evolution of quantum computing from 1990 to 2020 has a considerable average increase of connectivity in the network (growth of degree centrality measure), a moderate increase of the average inﬂuence of nodes on the ﬂow between nodes (little growth of betweenness centrality measure), and a little reduction of the easiest access of each node to all other nodes (closeness centrality measure). This evolutionary dynamics is due to the increase in size and complexity of the network in quantum computing research over time.

key_claims.claim: The QC research network is transitioning from hardware-focused to software-focused research.
key_claims.quote: This study also suggests that the network of quantum computing has a transition from hardware to software research that supports accelerated evolution of technological pathways in quantum image processing, quantum machine learning, and quantum sensors.

key_claims.claim: Quantum image processing offers high computing speed, low storage requirements, and high security for innovative applications.
key_claims.quote: such as in quantum image processing for creating quantum images because this new technology has high technical performance in terms of computing speed, low storage requirements, and high security [56].

key_claims.claim: Quantum machine learning and blind quantum computing represent important emerging technological trajectories in QC.
key_claims.quote: Other emerging technologies in QC research are quantum machine learning based on the interaction of machine learning programs and quantum algorithms [57] and blind QC, such that quantum servers do not have full information about activities that users are computing for high security of tasks.

key_claims.claim: QC research co-evolves through high connectivity, moderate growth in node influence, and reduced average access due to network expansion.
key_claims.quote: First, QC research co-evolves with complex interactions driven by three evolutionary characteristics: a) a high con- nectivity between nodes of research ﬁelds and technologies; b) moderate growth of the average inﬂuence of nodes on the ﬂow between nodes within network; c) a reduction about the average easiest access of nodes to all other nodes because of a larger size and complexity of QC network over the course of time.

key_claims.claim: Certain QC research fields like quantum algorithms and quantum information act as master entities in the network.
key_claims.quote: Second, some research ﬁelds and technologies in QC network have a critical position, playing a role of master entity for connections of manifold research ﬁelds and technologies, such as quantum algorithm and information.

key_claims.claim: R&D investments directed at high-connectivity QC technologies can support competitive advantage in markets.
key_claims.quote: This study shows critical research ﬁelds and technologies in QC that are growing with a higher DC measure; R&D management can allocate economic resources towards these research ﬁelds and technologies (e.g., quantum memory, quantum image processing, quantum machine learning, etc.) to support scientiﬁc and technological development that create a background for competitive advantage in markets.

key_claims.claim: Bibliometric mapping of QC has limitations due to query precision, data coverage, and confounding factors.
key_claims.quote: Although this study has provided some interesting, albeit preliminary results, as many other bibliometric studies, it has several limitations. First, the precision of the search queries is affected by ambivalent meanings in QC, such as information, computing, computer, etc. Second limitation of this study is that the sources under study may only capture certain aspects of the ongoing evo- lutionary dynamics of QC research. Third, there are multiple confounding factors that could have an important role in the dynamics of QC research to be further investigated, such as multiple discoveries [66], R&D investments, role of scientiﬁc institutions, collaboration intensity, intellectual property rights, etc. [67]–[73].

key_claims.claim: Future indices of technometrics based on network measures could help assess and predict technological change.
key_claims.quote: The future development of this study is also directed to design indices of technometrics based on measures of between- ness, closeness, and DC of networks to assess technological and scientiﬁc change, to predict the emergence of new technological trajectories, as well as to support further implications for the management of technology and R&D management.

open_questions.question: How do confounding factors such as R&D investments, institutions, collaboration, and IP rights influence the dynamics of QC research?
open_questions.quote: Third, there are multiple confounding factors that could have an important role in the dynamics of QC research to be further investigated, such as multiple discoveries [66], R&D investments, role of scientiﬁc institutions, collaboration intensity, intellectual property rights, etc. [67]–[73].

open_questions.question: How can the evolving and irregular borders of the QC research network be better characterized to identify stable technological trajectories?
open_questions.quote: Fourth, the network of QC research changes its borders during the evolution of science, and as a consequence, the morphology of network during the evolution, generating an irregular and complex shape, such that the identiﬁcation of stable technological trajectories and scientiﬁc ﬁelds over the course of time is a difﬁcult exercise.
